items.title: Rufus Reid interviewed by Monk Rowe, Atlanta, GA, January 4, 2013
items.q: And Stan Getz flipped it. They’re almost the same age too.

ctx.x: Well that was his — a lot of people thought that’s the way he played because he drank a lot. But that’s not it. He heard that. That’s the way he played. He kind of was laid back. Because I played with him when he wasn’t drinking at all. And he still played the same

way. And some people don’t really believe that, but it’s really true. He just heard that, the way that he phrased. And you can’t write it, you can’t transpose it, you just have to say, “Well just play this laid back.” Well what does that mean? But he was really consistent at that. So he heard that. That wasn’t something that — and the sound. It was just a full- bodied sound. I mean I’ve had a career with tenor players. And he was on the bottom. I mean he had this huge sound. And Stan Getz flipped it. They’re…
Well you just said something that makes me think about, is there such a thing as playing on top of the beat or behind the beat?
